title: Two-Person Invention · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Two-Person Invention · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose two players and a harmless everyday problem. One player proposes an imaginary invention and the partner explains how it helps. The group can identify the problem, the invention and its use. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: None.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Two-Person Invention, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The group can identify the problem, the invention and its use.
recall.why: The group can identify the problem, the invention and its use.
